Lake Sarmiento is included in excursion routes through Torres del Paine. Its shores offer views of wide expanses of water alongside the Patagonian steppe.

On a trip through the park, a stop at the lake is combined with views of the mountain massif, waterfalls and other lakes. Changing weather has a noticeable effect on the light and the visibility of the mountains.

## A Reservoir among Green Hills

Lake Suchitlán is the Cerrón Grande reservoir, created during the construction of a hydroelectric power plant on the Lempa River in the 1970s. It stretches between the departments of Chalatenango, Cuscatlán and Cabañas.

For travelers, Suchitlán is closely associated with [Suchitoto](/el-salvador/place/suchitoto/). After exploring the historic town, you can head to the water and see the islands and shores from a boat.

## Exploring the Lake by Boat

Boat trips and kayaking are available on the lake. Among the islands, El Salvador's tourism portal highlights Los Pájaros, Los Enamorados, El Chaparral and El Ermitaño. The exact route of a boat trip depends on the chosen itinerary.

Suchitlán is appealing for its combination of open water, islands and rural scenery. It is a place to enjoy a quieter part of the journey after city walks and archaeological excursions.

## The Lake on a Travel Itinerary

On the [“Best of El Salvador”](/el-salvador/tour/el-salvador-san-salvador-suchitoto-gulf-of-fonseca/) tour, a boat trip on Suchitlán is part of day four. It follows visits to Joya de Cerén and San Andrés and the transfer to Suchitoto. The lake is part of the tour's main route; transportation and the order of visits follow the program.

The Bolivian shore of Lake Titicaca is visited on journeys from La Paz across the Altiplano. The overland route leads to Copacabana, where travelers take a boat to the Island of the Sun.

The lake program combines a boat trip with visits to Inca monuments and the village of Yumani. This page focuses on the Bolivian side of Titicaca.
